analysis.title: Macro Roadmap: Cross Currents (23 Oct 2026)
key_insights: USD 10y rates have retraced just over 30bp from their highs as cracks appear in higher-yielding credit and equities rotate heavily. The AI vs AI-at-risk basket is down on the year.

AI capex has been central to the US outlook and the duration sell-off this year. The AI complex has now shown some sensitivity to higher yields, which caps sharp rate sell-offs. The left tail of a sharper AI downturn has fattened slightly.

With the recent equity-rates correlation, long duration is again a hedge for a long equity portfolio. A sustained larger rate rally needs a further fall in equity indices (not just rotation) or a sharper FCI tightening, which is not the base case.

A supply/demand imbalance drove US yields higher this year. Lower AI-related supply and portfolio hedging demand slightly reduce it but do not solve it. The imbalance persists unless the AI capex outlook collapses.

Fed: September inflation data would on most playbooks have pushed the committee toward an October hike. The Fed instead uniformly played down October, tilted toward gradualism by credit moves and equity rotation, and gave forward guidance.

GS base case is still a December Fed hike, but pricing is unlikely to return toward a full 25bp because the asymmetry favors receiving December as a hedge against further equity capitulation. The path beyond December is hard to call.
GIR sees US core inflation already through its peak, with tariff effects fading through next year and the AI inflation impact peaking by year-end, only 5bp more than the current impact.

ECB communication has not turned hawkish despite higher energy prices. European front-end rates sit in a tight range between weaker risk assets and growth on one side and higher energy on the other. EUR 1y1y implied vol is rich against benign realised vol.

GS sees ECB core inflation peaking in Q1/Q2 next year. Terminal rate pricing has historically peaked about 3 months after the core peak. The ECB keeps a gradual hiking path given FCI tightening and limited second-round evidence. Margins and wage settlements are the signal that would move it off a quarterly pace.

Today's Euro Area PMIs show input prices running ahead of output prices, suggesting firms are absorbing costs through margins. GS treats this with caution because of its weak past predictive power. The Euro Area MAP surprise index has fallen from its highs.
NatGas convexity into winter remains if temperatures come in colder than seasonal averages, but the asymmetry toward higher prices is less clear given the risk premium already priced.

France: the 10y OAT-Bund spread closed at 173bp on Thursday, the widest since November 2011, and France trades 45bp through Italy. The forced deleveraging of two weeks ago has stopped, yet spreads went through the 12-Oct highs, which GS reads as fundamentals, not just positioning.

Last weekend's protests in France were the largest since the yellow vests and the 2019/2023 pension strikes, and a post-protest poll puts Melenchon in the second round. GIR sees 2027 growth risks at 0.6% vs the government's 1.0%.

Even if the 5.0% 2027 French deficit target passes by year-end, GIR expects the deficit to realise at 5.3%. With 1% real growth, 2% inflation and a 4% borrowing cost, stabilising debt needs a primary surplus of about 1%. If funding costs converge to just above 5%, that rises toward 2%.

French front-end positioning has been reduced and changed hands at better levels but is still long. Further out the curve there is a lack of buying, even though fair value models screen OATs about 60bp cheap.

French event calendar skews to headwinds: Moody's review on 23 Oct, more protests this weekend, downside risks to Q3 GDP (first print 30 Oct), strikes on 5 Nov and a Melenchon rally on 6 Nov. Further widening risks becoming more convex, and this deters fair-value buyers for now.
UK: unemployment unexpectedly fell to 4.7% and payrolls rose. GIR tracks Q3 GDP at +0.7% qoq, slowing to 0.2% in Q4 and 0.3% in Q1. Inflation has been relatively benign with limited indirect effects.

UK: the market prices about 50bp of indirect effects vs about 100bp at the peak earlier in the year. Core has close to 120bp to go before peaking near 4% by end-Q2. About 110bp of hikes to terminal are priced, and GS prefers not to fade the front end, seeing upside skew to front-end inflation pricing.

UK Budget next week: event vol has decayed into it and consensus expects harder decisions pushed to next year's Spending Review. Headroom above the consensus 15bn or a lower gilt remit would be a constructive surprise. ASWs remain a favoured long.

Summary: AI and energy were both pushing rates higher for most of the year but now pull in opposite directions. Equities are now driving, and the forward distribution is wide in both directions even as central banks use gradualism to suppress vol.

tension_points.bull_case: Long duration is again a hedge to a long equity portfolio. The AI complex is now sensitive to higher yields, the left tail of an AI downturn has fattened, and credit cracks are appearing.
tension_points.bear_case: The supply/demand imbalance from AI capex issuance persists even if capex is trimmed, and a sustained rally is not the base case.
tension_points.what_invalidates: A sustained rally needs a further drop in equity indices (not just rotation) or a sharper FCI tightening. Without that, duration upside is capped, and the imbalance only ends if the AI capex outlook collapses.

tension_points.bull_case: Fair value models screen OATs about 60bp cheap, positioning has been reduced, and an energy-relief duration rally or lower vol could bring buyers.
tension_points.bear_case: Protests, a possible Melenchon second-round showing, weak growth and unforgiving debt arithmetic, with a calendar of more headwinds than tailwinds.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Fundamental improvement in the outlook is needed to turn buying momentum. Near-term headwinds are the Moody's review, Q3 GDP on 30 Oct, strikes on 5 Nov and the Melenchon rally on 6 Nov.

tension_points.bull_case: Weaker growth, cracks in France and tighter FCI argue for a patient, low-vol gradual path.
tension_points.bear_case: Higher energy prices and core inflation peaking only in Q1/Q2 next year could extend the hiking cycle.
tension_points.what_invalidates: First signs of second-round effects in margins and wage settlements would move the ECB off a quarterly pace.
